idiom_name: static class members behind typed instance accessors
implementation_notes: TypeScript inherits JavaScript's static members and adds a typed static side: a static property lives on the constructor (typeof LogSettings is the constructor type, while LogSettings in a type position names instances), so every instance of the class shares it and the compiler tracks it as part of the class's static surface. What replaces the classic structure is the static keyword plus TypeScript's separation of the instance type from the constructor type: private static level: number behind an instance getter/setter gives the pattern with the shared slot encapsulated and visible to the compiler. Prefer holding the state in an instance passed to the constructor whenever it must be swapped or faked - static state has no injection seam, and a module-scope let with exported accessor functions is the alternative shape when instances are not needed at all.
pitfalls: Static state is per module instance in the realm: duplicated bundles, worker threads, vm contexts and test module resets each construct their own class object, so the sharing never crosses realms.
Static members are not part of the instance type: code typed against LogSettings instances cannot see them, and a subclass that declares its own static member silently shadows the parent's slot.
Static initializers run when the class is evaluated (module load order), so a static property that depends on another module's static can observe undefined.
Tests share module state and there is no per-test reset unless the class exposes one; ordering dependence is the usual symptom.
